questions.question: When is a Python tuple hashable and usable as a dictionary key?

options.text: Only when all of its contained items are also hashable
Always, because tuples are immutable objects
Never, only strings and ints can be dictionary keys
Only if created with the namedtuple constructor

questions.explanation: If a tuple contains a mutable object (e.g. `(1, [2, 3])`), `hash(t)` raises `TypeError: unhashable type: 'list'`.
